Role_Team.positionality:
As an interdisciplinary doctoral student focusing on engineering and manufacturing construction, I have been consistently engaged in various online communities through regular usage of Reddit (<once per month>). My role as a PhD candidate equipped me with a solid theoretical grounding in cognitive science and technology-enhanced learning, allowing me to interpret the data collected from the crowd workers' narratives carefully. Despite my strong academic foundation, my personal experiences within the tech industry provide unique lenses through which I can view the nuances of the socio-cultural context in which this study operates.

The research questions touch upon several dimensions critical to our field—gender, race/ethnicity, age, educational attainment, degree subject, and subreddit usage. Gender identity informs both my professional and scholarly practices, while my educational background provides foundational knowledge that shapes my interpretation of data. Race/ethnicity reflects the diversity present within the population of crowd workers who contribute to this study, offering valuable insights into their lived experiences. Age plays a significant role in the dynamics of social interaction and information sharing patterns. My choice to be actively involved in multiple subreddits also introduces potential biases or preconceptions influenced by the community norms prevalent there.

These factors collectively contribute to the complexity of the research landscape, influencing not only the methods used but also the interpretations drawn from the crowd workers' descriptions. Understanding the intersectional nature of each dimension helps illuminate the multifaceted nature of storytelling in social media contexts, challenging conventional perspectives and revealing hidden complexities in the collective discourse. By embracing all aspects of my positionality, I aim to foster a more nuanced and inclusive understanding of the topic at hand.
